title: Grand Theft Auto VI Revs Up for a Worldwide Takeover
summary: More than a decade in the making, the newest installment of the video game franchise is set to bring in billions and set a new standard for the industry.

The year’s signature cultural event is expected to arouse the same fan passion as a sports championship, earn the eye-popping money of the biggest summer movie blockbuster and prompt the same obsessive study as a new Taylor Swift album. And it will all begin on Thursday when millions worldwide boot up their PlayStations and Xboxes to play what is likely the most anticipated video game ever.


Grand Theft Auto VI, the violent, frenzied franchise’s first new story in 13 years, has already reached 15 million pre-orders, according to the data tracker Sensor Tower. Should that number climb to 20 million this week, as many anticipate, then the sales will approach $2 billion. By the end of the year, according to estimates from Wedbush Securities, $3 billion and more than 30 million units is in reach.


“On Nov. 19, we will see the biggest release of any kind of entertainment I.P. in the history of humans,” said Joost van Dreunen, a business professor at New York University who[writes about the video game industry](https://superjoost.substack.com/) . “It sounds like an overstatement, but it’s up there.”


For those who do not play many video games, Grand Theft Auto VI — which returns players to Vice City, a nasty and brutish version of Miami — might seem like the juggernaut that came out of nowhere.


But for the franchise’s myriad fans — the ones who purchased more than 30 million copies of Grand Theft Auto V in 2013 and another 200 million copies in the years since; whose pre-orders are skewing heavily away from the $79.99 standard edition and toward the $99.99 enhanced version; who are making[a meme of calling in sick from work](https://www.reddit.com/r/AskReddit/comments/1xwvkgr/people_who_plan_on_calling_in_sick_the_day_gta_6/) on Thursday — the lengthy wait, the promise of best-in-class graphics and microscopic attention to detail, and the sheer mass of this monocultural moment have led to unprecedented hype.


The franchise by Rockstar Games is by this point far from the blocky graphics of its 1990s origins. Grand Theft Auto VI is a gargantuan, 200-plus-gigabyte universe (it takes hours to download) in which players will spend hundreds of hours partaking in reckless car chases and deadly gunfights, yes, but also following minor characters home to find framed photos of their dogs on their mantelpieces, surfing among bespoke in-game radio stations and exploring countless side quests.
